Scales

gives you a way to have control Start with same plot

weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax, color = name)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Temperature plot",
    x = "Minimum daily temperature (C)",
    y = "Maximum daily temperature (C)",
    caption = "Data from rnoa package; temperature in 2017"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(-15, 0, 15),
    labels = c("-15C", "0", "15")
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous (
    position = "right"
  )
## Warning: Removed 17 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_point()`).

#don't want original spacing, scale_x allows you to change it
#scal_y lets you do a transformation of data: eg "sqrt", "log", or "right
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax, color = name)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Temperature plot",
    x = "Minimum daily temperature (C)",
    y = "Maximum daily temperature (C)",
    caption = "Data from rnoa package; temperature in 2017") +
  scale_color_hue(
    name = "location") +
  viridis:: scale_color_viridis(
    name = "Location",
    discrete = TRUE
  )
## Scale for colour is already present.
## Adding another scale for colour, which will replace the existing scale.
## Warning: Removed 17 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_point()`).

#Defined mapping between the color variable and the name  
  #scale_color can edit color feature, can adjust hue
#scale_x - change title of caption
  #in scale if we want to change color of the name, can change caption to location (what all the locations are called)
#viridis package - scale color viridis assumes it is a continuous variable, have to specify discrete
  #viridis pallet: if you show this to someone who is color blind, it will be more accessible to them.

#Themes Where this lies on my plot doesn’t depend on difference between variable and color, just absent of data Grey background and white lines dont depend on data, just has to do with overall plot structure and appearance or theme

Shift the legend:

weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax, color = name)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Temperature plot",
    x = "Minimum daily temperature (C)",
    y = "Maximum daily temperature (C)",
    caption = "Data from rnoa package; temperature in 2017") +
  scale_color_hue(
    name = "location") +
  viridis:: scale_color_viridis(
    name = "Location",
    discrete = TRUE
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
## Scale for colour is already present.
## Adding another scale for colour, which will replace the existing scale.
## Warning: Removed 17 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_point()`).

Change the overall theme - on default ggplot uses grey and white -in changing theme wipes the slate and makes it brand new, if want to do theme minimal have to do the theme first

weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax, color = name)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Temperature plot",
    x = "Minimum daily temperature (C)",
    y = "Maximum daily temperature (C)",
    caption = "Data from rnoa package; temperature in 2017") +
  scale_color_hue(
    name = "location") +
  viridis:: scale_color_viridis(
    name = "Location",
    discrete = TRUE
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
## Scale for colour is already present.
## Adding another scale for colour, which will replace the existing scale.
## Warning: Removed 17 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_point()`).

Setting options

determine theme for every plot in document ggplot2.continuous. fill = “viridis” - will fill color for points later on all options ensure viridis color pallet and legend on bottom out.width shrinks it down a little bit: use this in the future of all markdowns to ensure that it will be there

library(tidyverse)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  fig.width = 6,
  fig.asp = 0.6,
  out.width = "90%"
)

theme_set(theme_minimal() + theme(legend,position = "bottom"))

options(
  ggplot2.continuous.colour = "viridis",
  ggplot2.continuous.fill = "viridis"
)

scale_colour_discrete = scale_color_viridis_d
scale_colour_continuous = scale_color_viridis_d
